DISCHARGE SUMMARY (SOAP) Patient: ___________ DOB: **/**/**** MRN: E-0093817 EARLY, HUNTER Admit: 09/01/2079 Discharge: 09/03/2079 Unit: Crisis Stabilization Unit Attending: Dr. Ayesha Karimi
S: 57-year-old man, voluntary admission after hearing gunfire near his apartment 08/31 and developing insomnia, hypervigilance and panic. Was seen same day at his annual physical where "reports of violence in the environment" was documented. Prior psychiatric hx: adjustment disorder seen by me 08/26/2078; GAD-7 3 then. No prior admissions, no suicide attempts. Denies SI/HI throughout. Alcohol light, no drug use. Mr. Early is married, lives in a third-floor apartment, previously worked as a forklift operator, now not working. He has been staying "early to bed" but not sleeping. Collateral from wife Margie: "he's not himself since the shooting."
O: Vitals stable. BP 115/98 on admit, 138/90 on 9/2, 121/84 at discharge. Wt 78.1 kg. Fasting glucose 121.5. MSE at discharge: calm, linear, mood "better", affect brighter. No psychosis. Insight and judgment good. Slept 6 hrs night of 9/2. Attended 4 groups. No PRNs, no restraint or seclusion.
A: Acute stress reaction to community violence, resolving; adjustment disorder; social isolation. Hypertension, prediabetes/T2DM and metabolic syndrome per PCP. Low acute risk of harm to self or others.
P: - Discharge home with wife 09/03/2079 11:00. - Follow-up Okonkwo LCSW within 7 days, psychiatry (me) in 2 wks. Housing authority letter re: safety requested. - Meds: no psychotropics started. Continue PCP meds (no changes). - Sleep hygiene. Crisis line given: 988. - Letter to PCP: cc Dr. Lindqvist, fax (570) 555-0150.
Dictated by Dr. Karimi; Ayesha Karimi MD Electronically signed 09/03/2079 12:05 Note routed to: Teodor Lindqvist; R. Okonkwo LCSW
